scopeNote: Interaction-level (Tier-2) verification of contract-profiler leads plus new cross-contract analysis. Oracle/AMM-rate divergence, flash-loan and pure economic realizability are deferred to econ-scanner per scope.

findings.law: Law 3 (owner footgun) + Law 1 (loss to later clients)
findings.description: emergencyWithdraw (base AYieldStrategy.emergencyWithdraw, onlyOwner, NOT nonReentrant, NOT whenNotPaused) delegates to _emergencyWithdraw, which transfers min(amount, heldShares) of RAW vault shares to owner() WITHOUT decrementing clientBalances or totalDeposited and WITHOUT pausing the contract. The principal ledger is left intact while the share backing shrinks, breaking the documented solvency invariant fairValueOfShares >= totalPrincipal.
findings.attackVector: No external attacker is required (owner-trusted action). The hazard is a *partial* emergencyWithdraw on a contract that is left live: (1) principalOf()/getTotalDeposited() now overstate recoverable principal (the ledger claims backing that no longer exists); (2) subsequent withdraw()/withdrawAsOwner() cap sharesToSell to the reduced availableShares (L351-354) but still debit the FULL requested `amount` from principal (L371-372), so the first clients to withdraw are made whole out of the remaining pool while later clients receive proceeds from a depleted share balance for the same principal burn -- a first-come-first-served drain; (3) any downstream consumer (e.g. stableYieldAccumulator) that reads totalBalanceOf/principalOf for its own accounting is fed an over-stated figure.
findings.impact: Loss is silently redistributed from later withdrawers to earlier withdrawers, and on-chain principal accounting becomes unsound until owner re-accounts off-chain. Because emergencyWithdraw is deliberately not pause-gated and does not pause, a competent non-malicious owner is not nudged to halt client activity first -- this is the non-obvious consequence that makes it a footgun rather than an obvious misuse.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Treat emergencyWithdraw as a terminal/migration action: pause() the strategy before calling it, or have the concrete impl proportionally reduce clientBalances/totalDeposited (or pull the FULL share balance only). Document that a partial emergency withdrawal on a live contract under-collateralizes remaining clients.

findings.law: Law 3 (owner footgun) + Law 2 (story: credited principal should reflect deposit)
findings.description: slippageToleranceBps is a single owner-set parameter that is OVERLOADED: it controls both (a) the AMM swap floor minOut and (b) the principal actually credited on deposit, via _creditedPrincipal(amount) = amount*(MAX_BPS - bps)/MAX_BPS (L213), which is then booked into clientBalances/totalDeposited (L322-323). setSlippageTolerance only validates _bps <= MAX_BPS (L195); there is no lower sanity ceiling. Raising the tolerance to absorb a wider AMM spread therefore silently haircuts the credited principal of EVERY subsequent deposit by the same proportion -- e.g. bps=2000 (a plausible 20% tolerance for a volatile/illiquid sUSDe Curve pool) credits only 80% of each deposit as recoverable principal; the missing 20% is permanently un-redeemable by the depositing client. At the boundary bps=MAX_BPS, creditedPrincipal == 0 and minOut == 0: a deposit swaps the full input to shares but books ZERO principal (the depositor's funds become an un-attributed donation to the surplus pool) while also disabling swap slippage protection (minOut=0).
findings.attackVector: No external attacker. A non-malicious owner reasonably treats 'slippage tolerance' as a swap-execution guard and does not expect it to also shrink the depositors' principal claims. The coupling is undocumented at the setter and unbounded above, so a moderate, well-intentioned tolerance increase silently under-credits client principal (loss surfaces only when clients later reconcile principalOf against what they deposited).
findings.impact: Silent under-crediting of client principal proportional to the configured tolerance; at extreme settings, total loss of deposit accounting plus disabled minOut. Engages Law 2 because credited principal no longer faithfully tracks the deposit, and Law 3 because the harmful consequence is non-obvious.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Decouple the swap slippage floor from the principal-credit haircut, or add a conservative upper bound to setSlippageTolerance (e.g. a few hundred bps) and document that the parameter haircuts credited principal.

findings.description: slippageToleranceBps defaults to 0. At 0, deposit sets minOut = convertToShares(amount) (the full vault-rate fair value, L308/L312) and withdraw sets minOut = idealUnderlying (full fair value, L357-358). A real AMM swap essentially never returns the full vault-rate value (Curve curve + spread), so EVERY deposit and withdraw reverts on the router's _expected floor until the owner explicitly calls setSlippageTolerance(bps>0). The contract is deposit/withdraw-DoS'd from construction.
findings.attackVector: No attacker; deploy-time hazard. The non-obvious part is the inverted semantics: a value of 0 reads like 'no/zero slippage protection (lenient)' but actually encodes the STRICTEST possible floor (demand perfect execution => always revert). An owner could ship the strategy, wire clients, and find all flows revert.
findings.impact: Availability only -- fails closed (no fund loss). Combined with CODE-002, the parameter's behavior at both extremes is counter-intuitive.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Require a non-zero slippage in the constructor or document the mandatory post-deploy setSlippageTolerance step.

findings.verdict: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED (Slither lastToken flag is a FALSE POSITIVE; validation-gap is real but low impact)
findings.description: setRoute validates only the path endpoints: path[0]==tokenIn (L71) and the last non-zero path entry == tokenOut (L74-80). It does NOT validate swapParams ([i,j,swap_type,pool_type,n_coins] coin indices), the pools array, or that the reverse route routes[tokenOut][tokenIn] is the true mathematical inverse -- swap() and isPairFullyConfigured() check only the reverse direction's .configured FLAG (L116, L128), not its contents. Slither's uninitialized-local on `lastToken` (L74) is a FALSE POSITIVE: the loop always runs and path[0]==tokenIn is already required non-zero, so lastToken is always assigned before the require.
findings.attackVector: No external attacker (setRoute is onlyOwner; routes are pre-computed off-chain from AMMRoutes.json). A wrong coin index / pool, or a B->A route that is not the inverse of A->B, passes endpoint validation and isPairFullyConfigured. However, the downstream blast radius is bounded: the Curve Router NG reverts on a genuinely invalid route, and the strategy always passes a vault-rate-derived minOut on every swap, so a bad/underperforming route causes a reverting or floor-protected swap (deposit/withdraw DoS), NOT a silent mis-delivery of value. There is no on-chain theft path under the trusted-router assumption.
findings.impact: Misconfiguration => failed or DoS'd swaps until owner corrects the route. Owner-trusted config item; flagged as an operational hazard, not an exploit.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Document that on-chain validation is endpoint-only; treat AMMRoutes.json correctness and reverse-inverse consistency as a deploy-time review gate.

findings.verdict: Slither incorrect-equality (L410) is BENIGN; an adjacent state-inconsistency is the real (low) note
findings.description: The Slither incorrect-equality at L410 (`totalShares == 0 || totalDeposited[token] == 0`) is benign -- comparison against literal 0 is correct. The reportable nuance: AYieldStrategy._executeWithdrawal resets the two-phase WithdrawalState to None and emits WithdrawalExecuted BEFORE calling _totalWithdraw (correct CEI for reentrancy). But _totalWithdraw only zeroes clientBalances[client] and decrements totalDeposited INSIDE `if (sharesToSell > 0)` (L417-431). For a client whose live balance is a tiny fraction of totalDeposited, sharesToSell = totalShares*clientStoredBalance/totalDeposited can floor to 0; the function then returns having moved no funds and left the client's principal on the books, yet the migration is recorded as executed and the state machine is reset. Separately, _totalWithdraw reads clientBalances[client] LIVE (clientStoredBalance, L414) and ignores the phase-1 cached `amount` entirely (used only for the amount>0 guard at L406), so a balance change between the 24h phases is silently honored.
findings.attackVector: Owner-only flow (totalWithdrawal is onlyOwner). No external attacker. Direction is benign (funds are NOT lost -- the un-migrated client retains full principal), but the owner may believe the migration completed when it did not, requiring re-initiation; and the cached-amount being decorative is a latent surprise.
findings.impact: Operational/state-handling only; no fund loss. QA-level.

findings.law: Law 2 (docstring vs behavior) -- value-leak claim refuted
findings.verdict: REFUTED as a protocol value-leak / cross-client theft; only a docstring-accuracy issue remains. Realizability of the upside as an arb is handed to econ-scanner but appears non-exploitable (see math).
findings.description: _withdrawInternal pays the recipient the full actual underlyingReceived (L367) but debits principal by the requested `amount` (L371-372), with minOut flooring the downside (L358) and no ceiling on the upside. Tier-1 (LOCAL-MKT-002) flagged the uncapped upside as a value that should route through skimSurplus, and (LOCAL-MKT-004-adjacent) framed the downside as 'accumulates as protocol yield'. Cross-contract/accounting verification REFUTES the value-leak framing for BOTH directions.
findings.proof: Let total shares S at vault price p (fairValue = S*p), total principal D, surplus = S*p - D, distributed to clients pro-rata. A withdraw of amount a sells a/p shares (convertToShares) and, at AMM price q, delivers (a/p)*q to the recipient while debiting a from principal. New state: S' = S - a/p, D' = D - a. Remaining surplus = S'*p - D' = (S - a/p)*p - (D - a) = S*p - D = surplus. The protocol surplus is INVARIANT under any withdrawal regardless of q, so remaining clients are unaffected: the upside windfall when q>p is the AMM counterparty over-paying on the withdrawer's OWN principal-sized share sale (not protocol surplus, not other clients' value), and the downside shortfall when q
findings.residual: The contract header comment 'any shortfall accumulates as protocol-owned yield' is INACCURATE for the AMM-slippage component: when underlyingReceived < amount due to AMM execution (not ERC4626 rounding), the shortfall goes to the AMM counterparty, and the surplus pool is unchanged (not increased). Recommend correcting the comment. The strategy's protocol-favoring rounding holds only for the convertToAssets/convertToShares dust, which is the real (negligible) protocol-yield accrual.

findings.law: Law 1 -- verified safe under stated trust assumptions
findings.verdict: REFUTED as exploitable. CEI is technically violated but no cross-contract, cross-function, or read-only reentrancy path exists under the trust assumptions.
findings.description: Both _depositInternal (state at L322-323 after the swap) and _withdrawInternal (state at L371-372 after both the swap AND the safeTransfer to recipient at L367) update clientBalances/totalDeposited AFTER external calls -- a CEI violation. Interaction-level analysis confirms it is not reachable as a reentrancy: (1) every state-mutating entry point (deposit, withdraw, depositAsOwner, withdrawAsOwner, skimSurplus, totalWithdrawal) shares OpenZeppelin's single-_status nonReentrant guard, so cross-function re-entry is blocked; (2) the only external calls during the stale-state window are to the trusted CurveAMMAdapter/Curve Router NG and to plain ERC20 transfer/transferFrom of underlyingToken and the vault share token -- none of which yield control to attacker code, because the registry trust assumptions exclude transfer hooks / fee-on-transfer / ERC777; (3) with no attacker callback, read-only reentrancy against the non-guarded view functions (totalBalanceOf/principalOf) is unreachable. The CurveAMMAdapter is itself stateless per call (pulls exactly amountIn, forceApproves exactly amountIn, router sends output to msg.sender) and holds no persistent funds.
findings.impact: None under the stated assumptions. Becomes live only if a token with transfer hooks is ever wired in (explicitly out of the trust model); retained as a documented latent assumption.

refutedLeads.1: REFUTED as value leak -> CODE-006 (surplus is provably invariant under withdrawal; upside is AMM counterparty overpayment, not protocol/other-client value).
refutedLeads.2: REFUTED as principal-invariant break -> CODE-006 (sum-invariant preserved; withdrawer bears own AMM slippage by design; docstring 'accumulates as protocol yield' inaccurate for the slippage component).
refutedLeads.7: REFUTED as exploitable -> CODE-007 (nonReentrant + non-hooked-ERC20 fully neutralize the CEI ordering; no cross-contract/read-only path).
